newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts can sue tobacco cos in state court.
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts can sue tobacco cos in state court.

text.p: A federal judge ruled that the state of Massachusetts can sue six tobacco firms in a state court for more than $1 billion, the state attorney general's office said on Monday.
In an order issued late Friday, U.S. District Court Judge George O'Toole stayed a tobacco industry suit seeking to block a suit by Massachusetts Attorney General Scott Harshbarger.
Harshbarger is one of 18 state attorneys-general trying to recoup taxpayer funds used to pay for medical treatment for tobacco-related illnesses.

Harshbarger's suit names Philip Morris Inc ; RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp's R.J. Reynolds Tobacco; B.A.T Industries Plc's Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp; Lorillard Tobacco Co, a unit of Loews Corp ; Liggett Group Inc, a unit of Bennett LeBow's Brooke Group Ltd, and two tobacco trade associations and two tobacco distributors.
His suit alleges the tobacco industry conspired to mislead the public by denying that cigarettes cause cancer and are addictive and by denying that nicotine levels in cigarettes are manipulated.
O'Toole's ruling did not dismiss the tobacco companies' federal suit but instead allowed the issue to be first decided by the state court, a tobacco company official said.
If federal issues remain after the state case, the matter could return to the federal courts for further hearings. the tobacco company official said.

"We're extremely pleased with the ruling," said Joe Helewicz, a spokesman for Brown & Williamson. "The industry sought to preserve the important constitutional issues for decision by the federal courts, if necessary, and today's ruling does just that."

Harshbarger said in a statement, "Judge O'Toole's ruling is a small but significant tactical victory that prevents the creation of a two-front court battle. It allows us to focus on holding the industry responsible to the taxpayers, who have paid the price for the death and disease caused by tobacco products."

Massachusetts Assistant Attorney General George Webber said the state is seeking more than $1 billion in damages based on the amount of taxpayer funds that have been spent on Medicaid and other programs to pay for smoking-related health care costs.
Eighteen states, plus the city and county of San Francisco, Calif., and New York City, are suing the tobacco companies.
